open_questions: Phase-curve amplitude 3372 ppm nearly equal to transit depth 3611 ppm and high chi2 35.57 dof 9 indicates spot modulation not fully characterised; radial velocities needed to rule out eccentric/stellar companion contributing to phase signal.

xgboost.planet_rank 0.17 is low, consistent with scorer down-weighting rotation-coincident signals and large phase-curve; similar TESS candidates with similar checks include four planets vs one not a planet, percent-coincidence only.
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a flat-bottomed 10.2 sigma dip every 1.45 days on the M dwarf and difference imaging puts the dip on the target with no neighbours able to mimic it. No secondary eclipse and no odd-even difference appear, and the 2.9 Earth-radius size is planet-sized. The 1.45-day period matches the star's own 1.44-day spot period and a strong starspot phase signal is present, but the transit shape, on-target centroid and single-sector stability still make a planet the best explanation pending radial velocities.

reasons.why: Planet-sized (undiluted depth 3615 ppm, rp_over_rstar 0.06013) favouring planet over stellar eclipse.
Single sector depth steady; no sector-to-sector depth change to explain signal.
Offset 1.769 arcsec (0.5555 sigma) on_target, suspects ruled out (>15 sigma), neighbours plausible_within_1px 0 despite 12 could_cause >46 arcsec away.
No secondary (snr 1.392 vs best_brightening_snr 6.532) and odd_even.diff_sigma 1.219 not significant, no binary signature.
Flat-bottomed (best_ingress_fraction 0.05) favours planetary transit over V-shaped stellar eclipse.

Period 1.45 d coincides with rotation 1.442 d (amplitude 23313 ppm, ratio_to_depth 0.9337) but phase_curve=3372 ppm chi2 35.57, dof 9 and fit_log_density_ratio -2.139 with star_density_penalty 134.7 share 0.7505 – period coincidence expected by chance but does not outweigh on-target, flat, planet-sized, no-secondary transit.
